decision.explanation: Initial priorities were the gain-centered Welch/estimator shapes, persistent time-frequency structure, cross-band envelope modulation and kurtosis distribution because these distinguish the references better than the nearly tied cyclic controls. The decisive evidence is Q01's clear nearest match to R01 in the baseline Welch distance and in estimator, cepstral, modulation-map, STFT, reassigned-STFT and wavelet controls, together with a shared approximately 3.5 Hz modulation family across several carrier bands [T01.estimators, R01.estimators, T01.cepstrum, R01.cepstrum, T01.modulation_map, R01.modulation_map, T01.stft_detail, R01.stft_detail, T01.reassigned, R01.reassigned, T01.wavelet, R01.wavelet]. Strongest counterevidence is Q01's much higher low/mid-band impulsiveness and its approximately 940 Hz cluster [T01.kurtosis_bank, R01.kurtosis_bank, T01.harmonics, R01.harmonics]. Envelope-only controls partly favor R03/R04 and cyclic distances are essentially tied, so those views are ambiguous rather than independent votes. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable for Q01 and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied [T01.orders, T01.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous]. On the supplied acquisition regimes, known similarity to C01 is supported, but the differing impulsiveness and spectral cluster prevent a claim of identical fault severity or component state.
